basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/PulumiCloudAuditLogs/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The Pulumi Cloud Audit Logs solution for Microsoft Sentinel enables ingestion of audit log events from Pulumi Cloud into Microsoft Sentinel through the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). It provides security monitoring and compliance auditing for infrastructure-as-code operations, covering authentication activity, organization membership changes, stack lifecycle operations, and access token usage. The solution includes analytic rules for failed login attempts, stack deletion, and organization membership changes. Pulumi documentation: https://www.pulumi.com/docs/pulumi-cloud/audit-logs/ Underlying Microsoft Technologies used: - Microsoft Sentinel - Azure Monitor Logs - Data Collection Rules (DCR) - Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) Dependencies: - A Pulumi Cloud organization on an edition that includes audit log export (Pro or above) - A Pulumi Cloud access token with permissions to read audit logs **Data Connectors:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 3 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for Pulumi Cloud Audit Logs. You can get Pulumi Cloud Audit Logs data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

link.label: Learn more about connecting data sources

options.text: This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

Detects when there are more than 5 failed Pulumi Cloud login attempts (user-login-failed events) from a single IP address within a 1-hour window. This may indicate a brute force attack or compromised credentials.

Detects when organization membership changes occur, including members being added, removed, or having their roles changed. These events are important for tracking access control changes to your infrastructure management platform.
Detects when a Pulumi stack is deleted. Stack deletion is a destructive operation that removes all infrastructure state. This may be legitimate maintenance or could indicate unauthorized activity.
